segments: Australia once sent its actual military to fight a giant bird and lost.
In 1932, 20,000 emus invaded Western Australia and started eating all the wheat. How do you stop a feathered army?
The government sent soldiers with machine guns to wipe them out. But what happens when the enemy refuses to line up?
The first ambush failed because the birds scattered instantly. How do you hit a target that runs at 48 kilometers per hour?
Their tough hides bounced bullets right off. Why did one machine gun jam just as a thousand birds gathered?
Major Meredith fired nearly 10,000 bullets with almost nothing to show for it. How do you explain that to the whole world?
Australia's military packed up in total embarrassment after losing a war to flightless birds.
Drop a comment if you think you could have outsmarted those emus better than the army did.

metadata.title: Random But True: The War Australia Lost To Birds
metadata.caption:
In 1932, Western Australia faced an invasion of 20,000 emus destroying vital wheat crops.

The government sent soldiers with machine guns to handle it, expecting a quick win.

The birds scattered instantly and could run up to 48 kilometers per hour, and their tough hides let a lot of bullets bounce right off.

When a machine gun jammed during the biggest encounter, Major Meredith had fired nearly 10,000 rounds for almost nothing to show for it.

The military eventually retreated in total embarrassment - officially, Australia lost a war to birds.

Drop a comment if you think you could have outsmarted the emus better than the army did.
